definition: Slang shortening of delusional, often used to jokingly accuse someone of being or acting delusional
explanation: The term delulu was formed through two linguistic processes: the clipping of “delu” from “delusional” and the diminutive reduplication of the “lu” sound to achieve a cutesy effect.

definition: Plump or chubby especially in an endearing way, usually used to describe an animal
explanation: Chonky is a broadening of “chunky.” While both terms have similar meanings, “chonky” has often been used in memes to describe animals like cats, evoking a more adorable effect.

definition: In the state of being in any sort of danger of failure, can be used in a similar fashion to "doomed"
explanation: If you’re cooking, you’re doing great, but if you’re cooked, you’re screwed. This is action bias, a phenomenon in which active verbs are more positive than their passive counterparts.

definition: A euphemism for autistic, sometimes used as an insult but can also describe atypical behavior in a more lighthearted way
explanation: Acoustic was coined as a joke among neurodivergent people before being adopted by other social media users as a light-hearted insult. Many in-group joke terms like “zesty” have undergone similar treatment.

definition: Amazingly good, very attractive, flawlessly styled; skinny, referring to the waist
explanation: Snatched originates from Black drag culture, as one might want to “snatch” the weave of someone who looks good. The term has narrowed to specifically describe women with skinny waists.

definition: A dainty, bubbly and hyper-feminine aesthetic, associated with bows, ribbons, frills and pastel colors
explanation: Coquette is a borrowing from French, and originally referred to flirtatious women. Through metaphorical extension, this definition inspired the name of the TikTok-famous aesthetic.

definition: Exciting, excellent, fun, cool; intoxicated
explanation: Lit has been used as slang for over a century. Recently, the term has shifted toward the definition of excitement more than intoxication, in an example of semantic drift.

definition: Similar to “out of left field,” describes comments deemed unwarranted, unexpected or wild
explanation: Out of pocket originated in AAVE before being popularized by Gen Z, with some theorizing that the term comes from playing in the “pocket,” or the groove, in music. Playing out of pocket is then considered undesired and disruptive.

definition: Crazy
explanation: Cray cray derives from the first syllable of “crazy” and is an example of reduplication, a morphological process in which a new word is created by repeating part of the original.

definition: Mid-tier, average, mediocre, not inspiring enthusiasm
explanation: Mid originated as a clipping from “middle,” though its recent popularity arises from TikTok videos making jokes like “It’s called the Midwest because every single thing in it is mid.”

definition: Used to describe someone who is aware of social injustice or advocates of social equality
explanation: The evolution of woke is an example of pejoration. After originating in AAVE as a positive term, it was co-opted by right-wing movements as an insult for progressivm.

definition: High quality, excellent; also used ironically to refer to weird or edgy memes
explanation: The original meaning of dank — “disagreeably moist and cold” — experienced reversal when applied as slang to quality marijuana and broadening to describe anything excellent. The term is sometimes used ironically, as in "dank memes."

definition: "Not safe (or suitable) for work," containing inappropriate or adult content such as pornography
explanation: NSFW is an initialism originally used to warn employees of adult content in the workplace. This meaning has broadened and is now used as warning for explicit content in many online spaces.

definition: Suspicious
explanation: Sus is a clipping from "suspicious" popularized by the video game Among Us. In this case, the affixation of “-y” onto an existing adjective turns “sus” into an even sillier form.

definition: A somewhat derogatory way of calling someone gay; effeminate or flamboyant
explanation: The slang term zesty is similar to the original meaning of the word — “appealingly piquant or lively.” The term experienced pejoration when adopted by non-queer people, similar to other in-group jokes like “acoustic.”

definition: Over the top; going beyond what is normal or appropriate, often in a dramatic manner
explanation: With origins in AAVE, the slang term extra is similar to several outdated uses of the same adjective. In the past, extra has also meant “excessive” or “extraordinarily good.”

definition: Legitimate, exactly as promised; can also be used similarly to “actually”
explanation: Legit is a clipping from “legitimate.” In addition to retaining the same meaning, the term has also shifted word class and become an adverb, similar to “legitimately” or “actually.”

definition: Sexually deviant; odd, bizarre, unusual
explanation: Freaky was formed via affixation with “-y,” a highly productive suffix that can be added to almost any word. The term has undergone narrowing, with the more precise definition of sexual deviance becoming the most common.

definition: Causing feelings of acute embarrassment or awkwardness
explanation: To cringe is to squirm from embarrassment. The slang version reflects a change in word category from a verb to an adjective, and has sparked concepts like “cringe culture.”

definition: Under the influence of a drug, especially marijuana; very stoned
explanation: The origin of baked as a synonym for “stoned” is unknown, though the verb “bake” itself may be a euphemism for smoking marijuana, as in the phrase “wake and bake.”

definition: Extremely ugly and unattractive
explanation: Fugly is a blend of “fucking” and “ugly,” first recorded in 1970 with a recent surge in popularity online. The word “ugly” derives from “uggligr,” which in Old Norse means “to be dreaded.”

definition: Out of date; trying too hard; skinny jeans, Starbucks pumpkin spice latte, almond millenial Christian core
explanation: Cheugy is a highly interpretable term, coined in 2013 by a high school student to disparage people who were off-trend. It was voted the American Dialect Society’s informal word of 2021.

definition: Not into fetishism or BDSM; alternatively, one perceived as plain, average or unadventurous in their choices or activities
explanation: Vanilla is a borrowing from Spanish “vainilla,” and the slang a metaphorical extension drawing on the plainness of vanilla ice cream, which then narrowed to refer to sexual preferences.

definition: Eating healthy food, supporting the protection of the environment, and loving the outdoors; hippie-like
explanation: Granola come from the prefix “gran-,” meaning grain, and the suffix “-ola.” In the 1960s, granola was common in the diet of hippies interested in healthy eating; now, the term has become slang for a similar nature-loving lifestyle.

definition: An attractive, confident woman, especially one who is a social media influencer
explanation: “Bad” is an example of a contronym, a word that has two meanings. In slang, its original meaning was reversed to praise physical attractiveness. The diminutive-creating suffix “-ie” was then added to make it a noun.

definition: One of my followers (or friends), particularly on Twitter
explanation: Oomfie is a diminutive of “oomf,” an acronym deriving from the Twitter term “one of my followers” or “one of my friends.” Twitter users often use “oomf” to refer to someone without identifying them by name.

definition: An opponent; any person on unfriendly terms
explanation: Opp, a clipping from “opponent,” originated in hip hop culture in reference to rival crews or artists. It has appeared in hip hop songs for decades before becoming widespread slang.

definition: “Non-playable character”; someone perceived as generic and lacking original or independent thought
explanation: NPC is an example of an initialism, referring to non-playable, background characters in video games. After the term broadened and became more prolific, real people seen as boring and generic have labeled “NPCs” as well.

definition: Something that causes a feeling of disgust or aversion towards something or someone
explanation: The exclamation ick may have been created through imitative etymology, copying similar words such as “sick.” In online spaces, the category of “ick” has shifted into a noun with essentially the same meaning.

definition: Slang term for style, charm or attractiveness; one’s skill in attracting a potential romantic partner
explanation: Rizz is derived from the middle part of the word “charisma.” It also functions as a verb, as in to “rizz up” a potential romantic partner — this process is called verbing or denominalization.

definition: An exclamation in reaction to seeing large buttocks; may also be used as a noun to mean a large butt
explanation: Gyatt has roots in AAVE. It may be an acronym from “girl your ass is thick,” or a derivation of “goddamn.” The term experienced semantic shift, evolving to refer to large buttocks, after being used by Twitch streamers and in the Skibidi Toilet parody song.

definition: The “greatest of all time,” used to praise successful individuals in a category of performance or activity
explanation: The acronym GOAT is quickly becoming an independent word, and while its origin is — for the most part — unrelated to the animal, it is often represented online using the 🐐 emoji.

definition: An ambitious and successful woman, especially an entrepreneur
explanation: Girlboss was conceived as a term of empowerment for women, but has possibly pejorated over time when used in contexts like “girlboss feminism.”

definition: Someone exceptionally skilled at applying rizz; an expert seducer
explanation: Rizzler is a blend of “rizz” and “riddler,” coined in reference to the Riddler from DC Comics. It was featured in a Gen Alpha TikTok song in the lyric, “Sticking out your gyatt for the rizzler.”

definition: The theft of food between friends as a “tax” on each other’s food
explanation: According to Twitch streamer Fanum, Fanum tax refers to friends stealing bites from each other’s meals as a “tax” on the food. “Fanum tax” is especially popular among Gen Alpha due to the Skibidi Toilet parody song.

definition: Something one thinks about constantly, such as a favorite franchise, celebrity, or meme
explanation: This catchphrase comes from a meme about men often contemplating the Roman Empire, and has since generified — someone’s Roman Empire can be anything they feel a deep emotional connection with.

definition: A singing human-headed toilet, as featured in the YouTube series “Skibidi Toilet”
explanation: Skibidi originated in scat singing as a nonlexical vocable — a non-word sound often found in music, such as “la la la.” Later, the word became attached to an animated head in a toilet in a dystopian YouTube series created by Alexey Gerasimov.

definition: A man who spends money for the benefit of a relationship with an often younger romantic or sexual partner
explanation: Sugar as slang for money dates as far back as 1862, while daddy is a colloquial term for a sexual partner, said to originate from prostitutes who used the term to refer to older men.

definition: A romantic or sexual relationship in which the parties involved do not clearly define their relationship as such
explanation: Situationship is a blend of “situation” or “situational” with “relationship.” It first appeared on a 2010 blog post describing a messy non-relationship, entering the mainstream in later years.

definition: Best friend
explanation: Bestie comes from affixation with the noun-forming suffix “-ie,” and it was first used in a London newspaper in 1991. Some people extend its implied meaning to apply to any friend.

definition: Any person, especially female, exhibiting an exaggerated sense of entitlement
explanation: Though its exact origins are unclear, the slang term Karen was initially used to ridicule racist white American woman. This definition has broadened to an insult for anyone, especially women, exhibiting entitled behavior.

definition: A highly self-reliant, assertive, dominant, and masculine male
explanation: Based on dominant “alphas” in wolf packs, the concept of “sigma males” as the archetypes of masculine men started on social media among gym bros. The term has since been co-opted by other demographics, and is now often used ironically.

definition: A member of the furry subculture, often one who enjoys dressing up as animal characters with humanoid characteristics
explanation: The exact origin of furries is unknown, but an early use of the word furry was in reference to fans of anthropomorphic characters at a sci-fi fan convention in 1980.

definition: A high level of charisma or presence
explanation: Aura first became prevalent in sports communities on TikTok and is a metaphorical extension of the original word, used to compliment people perceived as having a lot of presence.

definition: A man, usually in his late teens to twenties, whose traits may include a slim physique, a youthful and boyish appearance, and little or no body hair
explanation: The origins of the word twink are unclear. One proposed origin is an older British slang term, “twank,” referring to gay men who prefer dominant men as partners. Another proposed origin comes from the creme-filled cake snack Twinkies.

definition: A man who is unable to get a romantic or sexual partner despite desiring one, and blames women for his situation
explanation: Incel is a portmanteau of “involuntary celibate,” coined by a university student for a project on lonely people. In an example of pejoration, the term later became the face of an Internet subculture associated with hating women.

definition: A foolish person, a dummy, a silly goose
explanation: Tsundere girls in anime often insult their crushes by calling them baka. Online, the term has been used outside of Japanese, often somewhat ironically, as a synonym for “idiot.”

definition: A man’s penis
explanation: Schlong is a borrowing from Yiddish “shlang,” meaning “snake.” It is one of many object words that are euphemisms for a penis: “sausage,” “stick” and “knob” are some others.

definition: A woman who has many casual sexual encounters or relationships
explanation: Thot is an acronym for “that hoe over there,” credited to Chicago rappers in 2012. It was popularized and may have been pejorated by the “begone thot” meme in the mid-2010s.

definition: A fictional female character, typically from an anime, manga, or video game, to whom one is romantically attracted
explanation: Waifu is a Japanese doublet of “wife,” believed to have first appeared in the anime Azumanga Daioh. The term was adopted by anime fans to declare their love for certain female characters.

definition: An alpha male; an attractive, popular and sexually successful man
explanation: Chad comes from the Chad Thundercock meme and became a generified name for a stereotypical alpha male through the spread of “Virgin vs. Chad” and “Gigachad” memes.

definition: A racial epithet directed towards white people
explanation: Dating back before the United States itself, cracker — a word with many possible etymologies — initially referred to poor whites. It has since broadened to encompass all white people, with a surge in usage occurring due to Internet discourse.

definition: An older male friend, mentor, counselor, guardian, or paternal figure; an old person
explanation: Unc is a clipping from “uncle” that originated in AAVE and traditionally serves as a term of endearment for an older male relative. More recently, TikTok users have used “unc” to simply call people old, often as a light-hearted insult.

definition: To show excessive sympathy and attention toward another person in pursuit of affection or a sexual relationship
explanation: Gen Z popularized the term simp on platforms such as TikTok, but it actually originated in an American newspaper published in 1923 as a clipping from “simpleton.”

definition: To do something spectacularly well, often when it comes to fashion, artistic performance, or self-confidence
explanation: Slay originated as slang in Black, Latino and queer spaces and reached mainstream popularity via social media. The word has undergone semantic amelioration, developing a more positive meaning than “to violently kill” over time.

definition: To ejaculate
explanation: The origin of jizz is unknown, but it was first used to describe semen in 1888. It may have undergone verbing, also called denominalization, to later become a verb.

definition: To have sex without a condom; to do something quickly or recklessly, without prior planning
explanation: Rawdog is a compound formed from “raw” and “dog,” initially used to describe sex without a condom. After broadening, the term can now be used to describe any reckless activity.

definition: To manipulate someone using psychological methods into questioning their own sanity or perception of reality
explanation: The 1944 film “Gaslight” follows a manipulative husband who steals from his wife. The eponym gaslight derives from this film and gained popularity online in the 2010s, later surging in popularity in the 2020s.

definition: To withhold information or knowledge from others to keep something exclusive to oneself
explanation: The compound gatekeep originates from a sociological theory called “gatekeeping theory.” With metaphorical extension, it can refer to excluding someone from an in-group, such as a fandom, or simply refusing to share knowledge.

definition: To end communication or contact with someone without warning
explanation: The verb ghost is a metaphorical extension of one word’s meaning into another domain. Like spiritual ghosts that disappear at will, one who ghosts vanishes from someone else’s life on the Internet.

definition: To over-hype, praise, or compliment someone to the point where it becomes annoying or cringeworthy
explanation: Glazed donuts inspired the slang term glaze. Its first known use was in 2021, when a Twitter user quoted retweeted a photo of Donald Trump and Kyle Rittenhouse with “he glazing.”

definition: To respond to a post on social media with a greater number of likes, especially to condemn or mock the original poster
explanation: The concept of ratios began on Twitter and reflects the amount of likes and retweets a Tweet receives in comparison to replies. The phrase quickly became a verb through denominalization.

definition: To exhibit extreme nervousness, evasiveness, compulsiveness, erratic motion or excitability
explanation: Tweak, meaning to “pinch and pull, especially to the nose,” evolved into a slang term for snorting and abusing meth, which then evolved into a verb describing erratic behavior that seems like it could be caused by meth usage.

definition: To have sexual intercourse
explanation: The sexual version of smash likely emerged online in discussions of celebrities’ appearances, like in the “Smash or Pass?” trend, and continuously gained popularity over the last decade.

definition: To flatten the tongue against the roof of the mouth for supposed health benefits or a sharper jawline
explanation: Mewing is an eponym from John Mew, an orthodontist who suggested it as an alternative to jaw surgery. It exploded in popularity on TikTok, with influencers mewing to strengthen their jawline, and the practice soon became a meme.

definition: To perform the dab dance move, by moving both arms to one side of the body parallel with your head
explanation: Various rappers have claimed credit for the invention of the dab dance move, though it existed in Japanese pop culture as the “Sentai move” prior to the term dab being coined.

definition: To chatter constantly and excessively, often about something of little importance
explanation: Yapping originally referred to the high-pitched barking of a small dog. The term experienced semantic shift to arrive at the slang definition, which dates back to 1990s rap, though it became more popular on TikTok in 2023.

definition: A megafan, perhaps one whose fixation is obsessive, unhealthy or intrusive
explanation: Stan comes from an Eminem song about an unhinged fan named Stan, and may also be a blend of “stalker” and “fan.” Members of fandoms often label themselves stans to show their devotion as “super fans,” leading to some amelioration.

definition: To throw something with great force; to hurl
explanation: Yeet started out as a dance move before it detached from this definition and gained its new meanings through memes. It has often been used as a meaningless but humorous pseudoword.

definition: To publish personal information of a person without their consent, usually online
explanation: Dox is a respelling of “docs,” a clipping from “documents.” The term derives from the slang phrase “dropping dox,” a revenge tactic originally used by hackers to harass, threaten, embarrass or retaliate against their enemies.

definition: To be significantly more attractive than someone or something; to dominate in appearance
explanation: Mog comes from the initialism “AMOG,” which stands for “alpha male of group.” The term emerged in fitness forums, perhaps as incel slang, before entering mainstream use.

definition: To obtain something through trickery or manipulation; to handle or manage in a crafty, skillful way
explanation: Finesse is a denominal verb claimed to have originated in the Chicago drill scene. The meaning has experienced semantic shift, with recent popular usage of the word emphasizing trickery and guile while cheating in some way.

definition: To put someone down, or show disrespect by the use of insulting language or dismissive behaviour
explanation: Diss, a clipping of “disrespect” or “disparage,” likely originated in Jamaican English or AAVE. Rival artists and crews in hip hop often write diss tracks to attack one another in feuds.

definition: The act or an instance of flaunting something; something one considers impressive
explanation: The traditional definition of flex is “to bend or twist,” like when flexing muscles to display strength. This definition then broadened to the flaunting of other assets, like wealth.

definition: To behave in a submissive, subservient, or overflattering manner toward someone
explanation: Meatride is a compound and a metaphor for behaving submissively towards someone by “riding their meat,” often used by music fans to accuse others of meatriding their favorite artists.

definition: To take interest in something just to fit in with the crowd
explanation: “Jumping on the bandwagon” is a metaphor for following trends blindly, and was adapted into a verb through denominalization to call out disingenuous fans.

definition: To seek to enhance one's physical appearance
explanation: Looksmaxxing is a beautification trend involving practices ranging from skincare to cosmetic surgery. The term is combines “looks” and “-maxx,” clipped from “maximizing,” and the extra “x” in the infinitive form looksmaxx is an example of back-formation.

definition: To engage in sexual activity, possibly while or after watching a movie or a TV series together
explanation: Although the phrase “Netflix and chill” had innocent beginnings, it became a euphemism via Internet memes, undergoing semantic shift.

definition: Ugly, unattractive, rough-looking
explanation: Chopped has roots in AAVE, with some commentators tracing its origins to regional slang from the New York metropolitan area. Its usage dates back over a decade, but it recently entered the mainstream through social media virality.

definition: Awesome; used to express excitement, amazement, or hype
explanation: PogChamp is a popular Twitch emote used to express excitement. It gave birth to famous terms like “pog” and “poggers,” respectively examples of clipping and affixation. The term “pog” itself originated from the POG brand, a Hawaiian juice blend consisting of passionfruit, orange, and guava.

definition: Quirky, imaginative, or full of lighthearted, childlike wonder
explanation: The word whimsical has existed since the 1650s and derives from the term “whim-wham,” an archaic synonym for “knick-knack.” Its usage has skyrocketed thanks to the concept of “whimsy and childlike wonder,” popularized by the Internet.

definition: Aware of a supposed harsh truth about society; also can refer to skeptics of liberal or progressive values
explanation: In The Matrix, taking the red pill entails waking up from a simulation to confront a dystopian reality. The term was adopted by far-right movements, becoming a participial adjective via denominalization. “-pilled” was then extracted as a libfix that can be creatively combined with a variety of words. For instance, a lover of superhero movies may call themselves “Marvel-pilled.”

definition: Open minded; more specifically, open to casual one-night stands
explanation: Creator Sean Solo popularized the “Hongdae guy” meme, featuring a man from the Hongdae neighborhood in Seoul who approaches women to ask if they are open mindeu to sleeping with him. This version of “open minded” is an example of eye dialect, the use of nonstandard spelling to indicate dialectal speech.

definition: To be overwhelmed with more sensory input than the brain can handle
explanation: While its roots are in medical and psychological contexts, the term overstimulated has broadened through social media to become synonymous with “stressed” or “overwhelmed” for many.

definition: Carefree, cool, easygoing, indifferent, unconcerned
explanation: Nonchalant is a borrowing from French, and can be traced back to Latin, combining the prefix “non-” with “calēre,” meaning “warm.” Its popularity exploded through Internet memes, including the viral archetype of a “nonchalant dreadhead.”

definition: Lowkey, genuinely
explanation: Lowkirkenuine and its more popular adverb form “lowkirkenuinely” are blends of “lowkey,” “kirk” from Charlie Kirk, and “genuine.” The insertion of “kirk” is an example of infixation, similarly to “fan-fucking-tastic,” though in this case, it adds irony rather than intensified meaning.

definition: Fierce, stylish, confident
explanation: While calling someone a “cunt” is still generally considered an insult, positive renditions like “serving cunt” and cunty, rooted in Black and Latino ballroom and drag culture, are examples of semantic amelioration.

definition: Tough; impressive, cool, sometimes used ironically
explanation: Tuff owes its recent resurgence to social media, with both ironic (“bro thinks he’s tuff”) and unironic (“that fit is tuff”) usages. It likely originated  as an eye dialect misspelling of “tough,” appearing frequently in media such as The Outsiders.

definition: Weird, cringe, random, something that would only happen in Ohio
explanation: Ohio, the name of the state, experienced metaphorical extension to become an adjective encapsulating the bizarre quality of things that happen “only in Ohio.” Its use has been further popularized through the proliferation of slang phrases like “skibidi Ohio rizz.”

definition: Cheap, knockoff, of an inferior quality
explanation: Temu, a site famous for selling low-quality, mass-produced goods, became an adjective used to refer to things of similar perceived quality through metaphorical extension.
Commonly paired with a hand-weighing motion, 67 is an Gen Alpha inside joke with no fixed meaning, popularized by youth basketball players who went viral for shouting the number as a catchphrase.

definition: Washed up; someone who is past their prime and no longer relevant
explanation: The idiom washed up emerged in the 1920s, possibly alluding to theater actors washing off their stage makeup after finishing a performance. It was metaphorically extended to describe someone whose career is over or whose skills in a certain field are rusty.

definition: Admirable, praiseworthy; used to express approval of a person or opinion
explanation: Based originated from “basehead,” a slang term referring to cocaine addicts. Later, Rapper Lil B redefined the term as a compliment for unapologetic authenticity in an example of amelioration. The term became popular in online political circles and was co-opted by the far right before developing more neutral connotations.

definition: Done for, finished
explanation: Joever is a blend of “Joe” and “over,” initially used on 4chan as a humorous reaction to Joe Biden’s perceived defeat in the 2020 U.S. presidential election. The term resurfaced after Biden withdrew from the race in 2024.

definition: Low-quality, bad
explanation: Buns as slang for “buttocks” is a metaphorical extension on the rounded shape of baked bread, and was proliferated as a replacement for “ass” or “cheeks” in disparaging phrases like “that movie is buns.”

definition: A viral collectible plush toy with a toothy grin and large ears
explanation: The collection plush toy line Labubu was created by Hong Kong illustrator Kasing Lung and recently became a viral phenomenon, though Lung coined the term in 2015 as the name for a tribe of female elves in an illustrated book series inspired by Nordic folklore.

definition: A person who performs oral sex
explanation: Rapper Ice Spice popularized the usage of munch as a derogatory term for someone desperate to perform oral sex in her song Munch (Feelin’ U), though she did not necessarily coin the term.

definition: A handsome, fashionable, or otherwise attractive older man
explanation: While the origins of the term zaddy are unclear, some attribute its creation to fans of singer Zayn Malik, which would make it a blend of Malik’s first name and “daddy.” It may also be a product of AAVE.

definition: An unfunny joke that completely misses the mark
explanation: In basketball, an airball is a shot that misses the net entirely. With the help of memes featuring Stephen Curry shooting hoops from the moon, the concept was metaphorically extended to describe any total miss, particularly in the context of dating.

definition: An attractive person
explanation: While the term “fine shit” has existed for decades in AAVE, fine shyt is an example of algospeak, or coded language used to avoid content filters on social media. Another example of this phenomenon is the usage of “unalive” as a replacement for the frequently censored words “kill” and “die.”

definition: A traditional term of endearment for women, often directed towards male celebrities or fictional characters
explanation: The Internet’s take on the term babygirl is an example of metaphorical extension and narrowing, repurposing a common pet name for girls and women to apply to an archetype of grown man interpreted as secretly soft-hearted or adorable.

definition: Any person, pet, or thing, particularly one that is short, wide, and overweight; also used as a nonsensical filler word
explanation: Chungus is a blend of “chunk” and “humongous.” In 2018, the word rose to prominence through the proliferation of a stretched image of Bugs Bunny with the caption “Big Chungus.” Now, the word is often used ironically, like in the phrase “fuck my chungus life.”

definition: A young male individual who expresses himself through traditionally feminine aesthetics or mannerisms
explanation: Femboy is a blend of “fem-”, a relatively new prefix clipped from “feminine,” and “boy.” Although the term is typically used to describe individuals, some interpret it as a subculture or community label.

definition: A reaction used to express disbelief or laughter towards someone doing something foolish
explanation: “Sonion,” a blend of “son” and “onion,” originates from a meme of actor Anthony Mackie edited into an onion. Its popularity as an exclamation led to the introduction of sonion ring, a silly variation on the original inspired by junk food.

definition: A person with whom someone has an affair,  without being considered the main partner
explanation: Like the gendered alternative “side chick,” side piece has origins in AAVE and likely derives from the concept of a “piece of ass” on the side. Unlike most of its synonyms, it is a gender neutral label.

definition: A state of complete focus in an activity in which performance is heightened and feels effortless
explanation: The concept of “flow” was first named by psychologist Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi, metaphorically extending the sensation of being carried on water. The compound flow state saw a recent uptick in popularity through social media.

definition: An AI-generated anthropomorphic kentongan carrying a wooden stick
explanation: Tung Tung Tung Sahur was created by an Indonesian TikTok user following the Italian brainrot trend. The name may be connected to sahur, a pre-dawn breakfast consumed during Ramadan, with “tung” possibly drawing on the sound of percussive drums used for wake-up calls in an example of imitative etymology.

definition: A chemical scent released during heat to signal readiness for mating, featured in the Omegaverse
explanation: Omega pheromones were popularized as an Internet meme through viral jokes about secreting them, including a recent one targeting football player Jude Bellingham during the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

definition: An unappealing, lazy, messy person; a loser
explanation: Chud originated as an acronym for “Cannibalistic Humanoid Underground Dwellers” in the horror movie C.H.U.D. and was popularized as an insult for right-wing reactionaries. The term broadened to become more general, and some use it self-deprecatingly.

definition: A genre of fiction featuring romantic or sexual relationships between men
explanation: Yaoi is a borrowing from the Japanese acronym of “yama nashi,” “ochi nashi,” and “imi nashi,” respectively “no climax,” “no point,” and “no meaning,” a tongue-in-cheek reference to criticisms of the genre.

definition: A genre of fiction featuring romantic or sexual relationships between women
explanation: Yuri is a borrowing from the Japanese word for “lily.” The flower is a long-standing symbol of the genre; Korea and China use the semantic loans baekhap and bǎihé, both direct translations of “lily,” to describe such media.

definition: Low-quality entertainment to be consumed mindlessly; junk output from generative AI
explanation: The original definition of slop experienced narrowing to target AI-created content, and later shifted into a compound-forming suffix used to create terms like “friendslop” and “Kirkslop.” This spurred the antithetic development of the suffix “-gem,” which is often used to praise high-quality romance media as “yaoigem,” “yurigem,” or “hetgem.”

definition: Women, often in the context of dating; hoes
explanation: While its origins are in AAVE, the recent popularization of huzz is often credited to Twitch streamer Kai Cenat. The term itself is an alteration of “hoes” via the plural-forming suffix “-uzz.”

definition: A man’s penis
explanation: Dih is an example of algospeak used to bypass content filters on platforms like TikTok, though it is likely rooted in AAVE as a phonetic respelling of “dick.”

definition: A slur for robots, machines, and AI systems
explanation: Clanker has origins in the science fiction genre, notably featuring in Star Wars as a slur against droids. Recently, the term has risen in popularity amidst a wave of backlash against AI systems.

definition: A warning sign of a hidden danger or serious problem
explanation: Red flag as a euphemism for hidden danger is a metaphorical extension drawing on the use of bright red flags as a popular warning sign against danger.

definition: A stereotypical Gen Alpha child addicted to using their tablet or other electronic devices
explanation: The concept of the iPad kid was popularized by Gen Z users on social media platforms like TikTok. The nickname is often applied to children who throw tantrums when their iPad is taken away.

definition: A Glock; a hot dog; alternatively, a man’s penis
explanation: Glizzy originated as a blend of “Glock” and “-izzy,” an alternative form of the suffix     “-izzle,” which may have been used by African American girls in improvised chants while playing jump rope. The “hot dog” comparison exploded after memes started linking the size of an extended pistol magazine to a frankfurter.

definition: A term of endearment for a friend or partner
explanation: “Pookie” may have origins in German baby talk or the sound-symbolic association of “poo” with cuteness combined with the diminutive suffix “-ie.” While “pookie” has existed as an affectionate nickname since the 1930s, the phrase pookie bear became popular like platforms like TikTok more recently.

definition: To masturbate
explanation: Goon as slang for a hired thug evolved from “gooney,” coined by sailors to describe large, clumsy birds like the albatross. The term experienced denominalization and metaphorical extension to become a verb with sexual connotations.

definition: To make someone a cuckold by having sexual relations with their partner
explanation: The noun cuck is a clipping from “cuckold,” a reference to cuckoo birds who lay their eggs in other birds’ nests. Denominalization converted both forms into verbs.

definition: To insult someone subtly
explanation: The concept of “throwing shade” originated in Black and Latino ballroom and drag culture. The expression entered the mainstream through RuPaul’s Drag Race, and shade was denominalized to become a freestanding verb.

definition: To correctly call out a hidden motive; to notice, to figure out
explanation: Clock was popularized by Black and Latino queer communities in the context of recognizing someone as transgender, and the definition has since broadened.

definition: To have sexual intercourse
explanation: Cracking as slang for sex emerged on social media, with some criticizing the misogynistic undertones of using it to describe penetrative sex with a woman. However, this definition has largely broadened to refer to sex in general.

definition: To betray or kill someone
explanation: “Slime,” a term of endearment used in AAVE, evolved through denominalization and pejoration into the concept of sliming out someone else. Recently, the phrase gained attention when Drake and SZA used it in the song Slime You Out.

definition: To present a good look; to nail an attitude or performance
explanation: The concept of serving is rooted in Black and Latino queer culture, inspired by ballroom and drag scenes in which performers “deliver” their looks and performances.

definition: To assassinate
explanation: The verb kirk is an eponym commemorating the late political commentator Charlie Kirk, constituting one of many recently developed Kirk-inspired terms.

definition: To pretend to be a part of a movement or group; to fake an interest
explanation: Larp, originally an acronym for “live-action roleplaying,” broadened via metaphorical extension to describe inauthentic behavior or posturing.

definition: To delay an orgasm on purpose for sexual stimaultion; to frustrate by constantly delaying something
explanation: The name for the sexual practice of edging derives from a metaphorical extension on bringing someone to the “edge” of an orgasm. The term experienced broadening upon arriving on social media platforms.

definition: To do or say something for the purpose of looking cool
explanation: The compound verb aurafarm repurposes the practice of “farming” loot in video games via metaphorical extension to the idea of cultivating coolness in social situations.

definition: To excessively consume digital content, particularly content that elicits negative emotions
explanation: Doomscroll is a compound referencing the feeling of impending doom caused by continually reading bleak news. The term skyrocketed in usage as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic.

definition: To intentionally cause anger for content or for fun
explanation: The compound ragebait originated as a descriptor for a specific genre of content, with the suffix “-bait” mirroring its function in the older term “clickbait.” It has since experienced denominalization and broadening, entering everyday usage as a verb.

definition: To heavily edit a photo with glam styling beauty filters
explanation: Yassify was coined via back-formation from “yassification,” which first appeared on Twitter as a synonym for “beautification.” The expression “yass” is an eye dialect spelling of “yes,” popularized by AAVE and queer slang.

definition: To explain something condescendingly, especially when the listener already knows
explanation: Mansplain is a blend of “man” and “explain,” highlighting its origins as a callout towards men who assume women have an inferior understanding of certain subjects due to their gender.

definition: To stand with one’s arms held out horizontally at shoulder height, forming a T with the body
explanation: The term T-pose is an example of iconicity, in which form of the word resembles its meaning. The pose is a common default for humanoid models in video games, and it entered meme culture in the 2010s through jokes about standing in the position to assert dominance.

definition: To act out recklessly, often in reaction to something angering or frustrating
explanation: The phrase crash out emerged from AAVE and can be traced to lyrics by rapper NBA YoungBoy. It is an example of a phrasal verb, a common structure in English that combines a base verb with a particle to mark a new verb.

definition: To edit a person or object with Charlie Kirk’s face
explanation: Kirkify is a verb derived from “kirk,” the last name of the late political commentator Charlie Kirk, and the suffix “-ify,” referencing post-assassination memes of Kirk created using face-swapping technology.

definition: To obtain money or property illicitly
explanation: Grift is an alteration of “graft,” meaning “a dishonest gain or bribe,” which is theorized by some to be a metaphorical extension on an alternative definition of the word associated with digging. In recent political discourse, commentators seen as inauthentic or possibly paid off are often labeled as “grifters.”

definition: To spend time outside, away from the Internet
explanation: Touch grass is often used in the imperative as a suggestion to someone perceived as “out of touch” with reality. The phrase is a metaphorical extension converting the act of making physical contact with a plant into a figurative command to go outside.

definition: To use clownish antics to attract romantic attention
explanation: Jestermaxxing emerged from incel slang on looksmaxxing forums. The term combines “jester” and “-maxx,” a clipping of “maximizing” converted into a suffix through the popularity and memeification of looksmaxxing.
